unlisted_practices: Develop a clinical-reliability annotation schema for preference data that specifies when a candidate response should challenge rather than affirm an apparently distorted account, with attention to psychosis, mania, secondary gain, and crisis presentations.

Involve clinicians, including psychiatry and clinical psychology experts, in preference labeling, red-team scenario design, and postmarket live-conversation auditing for AI assistants used in or affecting mental health contexts.
Add explicit AI-use items to standard psychiatric history-taking proformas and include AI-use inquiry competencies in medical curricula.

Add clinical reliability of self-report as a data-quality criterion to trustworthy-AI frameworks and regulatory conformity assessment so that training and preference data for mental-health-relevant systems are assessed for systematic biases that undermine self-report reliability.
Subject clinician-input schemes for data curation and preference labeling to governance, including lived-experience representation, transparent criteria, and external audit.

screen.reason: This is a Viewpoint / conceptual synthesis paper proposing recommendations and a governance framework regarding the clinical reliability of training/preference data to prevent AI collusion in mental health applications.
